documents.title: Psychiatry progress letter
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
To the primary care physician,

This is to update you on our mutual patient. After adequate trials of risperidone (April to September 2023) and aripiprazole (September 2023 to January 2024), she continued to have persistent auditory hallucinations and persecutory ideas. On 01/09/2024 aripiprazole was discontinued and clozapine was started with a standard titration. She reached 300 mg at bedtime on 02/02/2024 and remains on that dose.

Absolute neutrophil counts are being drawn through our clinic's laboratory per the clozapine monitoring schedule, weekly for now; results to date are normal. We will copy you periodically.

We would appreciate continued metabolic monitoring on your end (weight, A1c, lipids). Please let us know of any fever, sore throat or signs of infection you see, as those need an ANC the same day.

Outpatient Psychiatry

documents.title: Med list updated from psychiatry letter

conditions.label: Tay-Sachs disease carrier status with indicated partner screening

documents.title: Gynecology - Preconception Counseling
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
OBSTETRICS & GYNECOLOGY - RETURN VISIT
Date of service: 02/12/2024
Visit type: preconception counseling

She returns, last seen here in August for genito-pelvic pain. She and her husband would like to start a family. Her ancestry is Ashkenazi Jewish and she is worried about inherited disease, above all the chance that a child of hers could be affected by Tay-Sachs; a cousin was diagnosed with it. Her husband, 30, is of mixed European ancestry and knows of no genetic conditions in his family. He attended the visit and asked what comes next.

History: schizophrenia, currently on clozapine; high myopia, degenerative type; genito-pelvic pain/penetration disorder evaluated here.
Medications: clozapine 300 mg at bedtime.
Allergies: NKDA.
ROS: no complaints.
Exam: unremarkable.

Genetic testing: carrier testing for Tay-Sachs disease identified a pathogenic HEXA variant. She is a heterozygous carrier.

Counseling: As a carrier she is not expected to have symptoms. A child would be at risk only if her partner is also a carrier; in that case each pregnancy would carry a 1 in 4 chance of an affected child. Carrier screening of her husband is recommended before conception. Options if both are carriers were reviewed in general terms. They will contact our genetics counselor to arrange his testing.

Obstetrics & Gynecology

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up. Now on clozapine since January (psych letter 2/7), 300 mg at bedtime. She is sleeping a lot at first, less now. Voices "come and go," still there. Psychiatry draws her neutrophil counts; she goes to their lab every week.

Gyn letter from the February preconception visit came 3/20: Tay-Sachs carrier, husband to be screened. She says he has not had his test yet, insurance paperwork. No pregnancy yet.

Meds: clozapine 300 mg qhs (psych). NKDA.

Exam: vitals normal, weight 64 kg, up a little more. Calm, affect restricted, organized today. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. No tremor.

A/P
1. Schizophrenia on clozapine, psychiatry managing and doing ANC. Metabolic labs today: A1c, lipids, BMP; CBC with diff since we are drawing anyway.
2. Tay-Sachs carrier status. Added to problem list. Partner screening through gyn genetics.
3. Situational anxiety, GAD-7 7, a bit better.
4. Weight up about 3 kg in a year on antipsychotics; reviewed meals and walking, she and her sister walk most evenings.

RTC 6 months / physical in fall.

documents.title: Ophthalmology Follow-up
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
Ophthalmology - follow-up exam 06/19/2024

Interval: no change in vision with current glasses. No flashes, new floaters or curtain.
Meds: clozapine 300 mg nightly.

Best corrected acuity 20/30 right and left with her current -7.00 D correction; manifest refraction unchanged. Pressures normal. Anterior segments quiet.
Dilated exam: myopic tessellated fundi with thin pale discs, unchanged from last year. Full peripheral exam both eyes without tears, holes or detachment.

Impression: degenerative high myopia, stable.
Plan: continue current spectacles. Dilated exam in one year, sooner with any detachment symptoms, which were reviewed again with her.

Ophthalmology

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN RECORD
Arrival 08/10/2024 16:25

Chief complaint: abdominal pain, severe.

HPI: 29 year old woman with schizophrenia on clozapine. Abdominal pain for two days, steadily worse. Appears anxious. Requested pain medication repeatedly during the visit; after analgesics she continued to rate the pain as severe.

Past history as given by patient: several prior admissions at other hospitals for joint pain, chest pain and on-and-off diarrhea, never with a firm diagnosis despite extensive testing. States she had an exploratory abdominal operation at another hospital but cannot name it or provide records.
Medications: clozapine 300 mg qhs.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: never smoker, no alcohol, unemployed.

Exam: vitals per nursing flowsheet, unremarkable. Abdomen soft, mild diffuse tenderness without rebound or guarding. A small well-healed lower abdominal scar, which she attributes to the surgery above. Remainder of exam unremarkable.

Results: Hgb 13.2, WBC 7.0, platelets 250. Amylase 45 and lipase 50, both normal. Liver tests within normal limits. Urinalysis normal.

Course: Comparison with outside records obtained during the visit showed inconsistencies between the histories she has given at earlier admissions. Emergency psychiatry was consulted; her presentation was felt to be most consistent with factitious disorder imposed on self. No acute surgical or medical process identified. Findings discussed with the patient in a nonconfrontational way.

Impression: 1. Abdominal pain, no acute cause found. 2. Factitious disorder imposed on self.
Disposition: discharged home with her sister. Follow up with primary care and her psychiatrist.

Emergency Medicine

documents.title: Office Visit - ED Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-ED. On 8/10 she went to the ED for two days of severe belly pain; told bloodwork was normal and sent home that night. Pain went away over the following days. Eating, bowels at baseline, no fever, no vomiting, no urinary symptoms. She did not bring discharge paperwork and does not remember what they said beyond normal labs.

On clozapine 300 mg qhs, taking it with her sister's help. Psych visits continue.

Exam: afebrile, vitals normal. Comfortable. Abdomen soft, nontender, no masses, normal bowel sounds.

A/P: Abdominal pain, resolved, workup reportedly negative. No further testing. Requesting the ED record. Return if it recurs.

Physical due in the fall.

documents.body: Trivalent flu 0.5 mL IM left arm and 2024-25 COVID 0.3 mL IM right arm. Afebrile, no sore throat or illness today (asked given clozapine). Talked her through each step ahead of time, which she said helps. Observed 15 minutes, no reaction.

documents.title: Annual Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical.

ED record from August arrived 9/16 after a second request. Workup for the abdominal pain negative (Hgb 13.2, WBC 7.0, amylase and lipase normal, LFTs and UA normal). ED and their psychiatry consultant documented factitious disorder imposed on self, noting inconsistencies with outside admissions for joint pain, chest pain and diarrhea; none of those were reported to us at intake and none are in the prior-practice records. She also gave the ED a history of an abdominal operation elsewhere; we have no surgical history on file. I raised the ED's findings with her gently today. She listened, said little, did not want to discuss it further. Psychiatry is aware per the ED record.

Psych: clozapine 300 mg qhs, stable for a few months now by her and her sister's account, fewer voices. Weekly lab visits for ANC at psychiatry, recently spaced out.

Eyes: ophthalmology letter June, stable high myopia, no tears.

Gyn: husband still hasn't had carrier screening. They are holding off on pregnancy for now.

Meds: clozapine 300 mg qhs. NKDA. Never smoker, no alcohol.

Exam: vitals normal, weight 65 kg. Calm, organized, affect restricted. Glasses. Thyroid normal size. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender; small healed lower abdominal scar. No edema.

PHQ-9 3, GAD-7 6.

A/P
1. Health maintenance. Pap overdue; she again prefers to wait. Vaccines done in October.
2. Schizophrenia on clozapine, improving. CMP, lipids, A1c, TSH today.
3. Factitious disorder imposed on self, per ED and emergency psychiatry. Added to problem list. Plan: one primary care physician, consistent follow-up, avoid unnecessary testing, coordinate with psychiatry.
4. Situational anxiety, stable.
5. Tay-Sachs carrier, partner screening pending on their end.
6. Degenerative high myopia, yearly ophthalmology.

RTC 6 months.
